papers.title: Nonlinear Aging of the Human TCR Repertoire Is Influenced by Sex, CMV, and Cancer.
papers.authors: Lange N, Attermann AK, Juul RI, Andersen L, Nordentoft I, Jessen LE, McGranahan N, Aerts HJWL, Dyrskjøt L, Birkbak NJ.
papers.abstract: Aging is accompanied by a progressive decline in immune function, increasing susceptibility to infections, cancer, and poorer treatment outcomes. The diversity of the T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire, reflecting the capacity to recognize diverse antigens, is known to decline with age. However, how intrinsic and extrinsic factors jointly shape TCR diversity and its rate of decline, as well as the extent to which this diversity influences clinical outcomes in cancer, remain poorly characterized. Here, we integrate TCR sequencing data from 1.32 billion unique T cell clones, derived from 798 patients with cancer and 5052 individuals without cancer across 14 independent cohorts, to systematically characterize the effects of age, sex, and chronic cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection on peripheral blood repertoire diversity. We identify a nonlinear trajectory of diversity loss that accelerates after midlife, with a marked increase in the rate of decline beyond approximately 50 years of age, which is further modified by sex and CMV infection. In patients with cancer, higher peripheral TCR diversity was associated with improved overall survival across multiple cancer types, even when accounting for the impact of age, sex, and CMV on diversity. Together, these findings underline peripheral TCR repertoire diversity as a dynamic marker of immune aging shaped by demographic and chronic viral factors.

papers.title: Genetic Prioritization of BTN3A2 Reveals an Interferon-Responsive T-Cell Program in Dermatomyositis Through Single-Cell Mendelian Randomization and Multi-Omics Integration.
papers.authors: Jin J, Di Y, Zhang X, Sun S, Chen M, Guo Z, Wang H, Dai S.
papers.abstract: Dermatomyositis (DM) is a complex autoimmune disorder characterized by genetic susceptibility and dysregulated immune activation. However, the relationship between genetic variation and specific immune cell states remains poorly understood. We aimed to identify genetically supported immune-cell-specific molecular programs underlying DM and investigate their biological relevance. We integrated immune-cell-specific single-cell expression quantitative trait loci (sc-eQTLs) from the OneK1K cohort with DM genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). Candidate genes were replicated using an independent sc-eQTL dataset and prioritized by Bayesian colocalization. Multi-tissue validation was performed using skeletal muscle transcriptomics, peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC), and skin single-cell RNA sequencing, protein expression data, clinical phenotypes, virtual knockout analysis, and gain-of-function analyses of BTN3A2. We identified 204 immune cell-specific eGenes associated with DM and prioritized four high-confidence genes, including HLA-DRB1, HLA-C, Lnc-HLA-B-2, and BTN3A2. BTN3A2 showed robust colocalization across multiple CD4 + and CD8 + T-cell subsets and was further supported by muscle transcriptomic data. BTN3A2 was consistently upregulated in both DM muscle tissues and PBMCs and was broadly expressed across T-cell, NK-cell, and B-cell populations. BTN3A2 + T cells exhibited enhanced cytotoxic, activation, antigen-presentation, and interferon-responsive programs, which were reproduced in circulating PBMCs and lesional skin T cells. BTN3A2 expression was negatively correlated with MMT8 scores, while in silico knockout analysis implicated interferon-stimulated and antiviral pathways. Integrating cell-type-specific genetic evidence with multi-tissue immune profiling identified BTN3A2 as a genetically supported candidate associated with DM and an interferon-responsive T-cell state, providing novel insights for future mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: MEK1/2 Signalling establishes an alloreactive effector T cell program through SMAD4 during cardiac allograft rejection.
papers.authors: Zhao J, Ran S, Zhou S, Li Y, Zhan W, Lai L, Cui J, Xia J, Wu J.
papers.abstract: Background Acute allograft rejection is largely dependent on T cell-driven immune responses; however, the molecular programs that establish and maintain effector T cell states during rejection remain incompletely defined. Methods Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was conducted to characterize the activation of signalling pathways in T cells during acute allograft rejection. The function of MEK1/2 signalling was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo using mice with targeted deletion of Mek1/2 in T cells and pharmacological inhibition. Phosphoproteomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining, and western blotting were conducted to investigate downstream signalling mechanisms, particularly those involving SMAD4. Results Effector CD4 and CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced MEK/ERK pathway activation throughout the rejection process. MEK1/2 inhibition, either via genetic deletion or pharmacological blockade, attenuated T cell activation and effector activity, leading to reduced rejection and prolonged graft survival. Phosphoproteomic analysis identified SMAD4 as a key downstream effector of MEK1/2 signalling. Mechanistically, MEK1/2 deficiency reduced SMAD4 nuclear translocation in activated T cells, accompanied by diminished effector T cell responses. Conclusions MEK1/2 signalling regulates T cell activation and effector phenotypes via SMAD4 nuclear translocation in heart transplant rejection. Therapeutic intervention targeting this pathway may contribute to alloimmune response regulation and improve transplant outcomes.

papers.title: Peripheral CD4 + T-Cell Reserve as a Potential Biomarker of CD20 × CD3 Bispecific Antibody Outcomes and BTK Inhibitor-Associated Immune Modulation in B-Cell Lymphoma.
papers.authors: Yu H, Chai J, Cao J, Hu D, Jin Z, Li Y, Lv J, Chen J, Wang Y, Zhang W, Zhu J, Song Y.
papers.abstract: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) targeting CD20 × CD3 have achieved remarkable efficacy in relapsed or refractory (R/R) B-cell lymphoma, yet clinical responses remain heterogeneous and predictive biomarkers are lacking. We retrospectively evaluated associations between peripheral immune profiles and outcomes in 40 patients treated with CD20 × CD3 BsAbs and explored BTK inhibitor-associated immune changes using a paired BTK inhibitor cohort, functional assays, mouse models, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Higher baseline CD4 + T-cell counts correlated with superior response rates and prolonged progression-free survival, whereas CD8 + counts showed no association. Elevated CD4 + T-cell levels were linked to increased activation of effector CD8 + CD28 + T cells and greater induction of IL-2 and IFN-γ following treatment. Across paired clinical samples and experimental models, BTK inhibition was associated with CD4 + T-cell expansion and enhanced T/NK-cell proliferative and cytotoxic signatures. In an exploratory real-world observation, three patients received BTK inhibition before glofitamab; all achieved complete responses, with two remaining in remission at data cutoff and one relapsing after 8.4 months. These findings identify peripheral CD4 + T-cell reserve as a potential biomarker associated with BsAb outcomes and provide a rationale for further investigation of BTK inhibitor-mediated immune modulation in BsAb treatment strategies.

papers.title: Single-cell transcriptome atlas reveals a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense against Sclerotium rolfsii in Dendrobium officinale.
papers.authors: Li L, Xu Y, Liu W, Niu Z, Xue Q, Ding X.
papers.abstract: Plants employ cell-type-specific transcriptional programs to defend against pathogens, yet the cellular heterogeneity of immune responses in the medicinal orchid Dendrobium officinale Kimura et Migo remains largely unexplored. A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the D. officinale stem base upon Sclerotium rolfsii infection was constructed, profiling over 20 000 cells across 12 and 24 h post-infection. A total of 21 cell clusters were resolved into 6 major cell types-epidermal, ground tissue parenchyma, proliferating, xylem, phloem, and vascular bundle parenchyma cells-with identities validated by fluorescence in situ hybridization. Cell-type-specific analyses revealed that epidermal and phloem cells mounted early defense responses, while xylem cells exhibited the most extensive transcriptional reprogramming at 24 hpi, coinciding with the activation of lignin biosynthesis pathways. WRKY33 was identified as a central transcriptional activator that directly binds W-box motifs in the promoters of lignin biosynthetic genes C4H and HCT, promoting lignin deposition and enhancing disease resistance. Conversely, the nuclear-localized chaperone HSP81 physically interacts with WRKY33 and functions as a broad regulator of multiple transcription factors via co-factor sequestration, thereby compromising defense when overexpressed. These findings uncover a WRKY33-HSP81 regulatory module that orchestrates phenylpropanoid-mediated defense in D. officinale, providing a high-resolution cellular framework for understanding plant immunity and offering potential targets for improving disease resistance in this economically valuable species.

papers.title: Sphingosine-1-Phosphate Attenuates LPS-Induced Inflammatory Cardiac Injury in Association With RASGRP1-S100A9-NLRP3 Signaling.
papers.authors: Yue C, Li Q, Li C, Yang T, Huang X, Yue F, Long Q, Li R, Lei R, Ma Q, Hu C, Yang Q, Yan Y, Liu Y, Yan Q, Yang M.
papers.abstract: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) induces endotoxemia-associated inflammatory cardiac injury rather than classical viral or autoimmune myocarditis. Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) regulates cardiovascular and immune responses, predominantly through S1P receptors, but whether it also modulates macrophage-associated inflammatory signaling during LPS-induced cardiac injury remains incompletely understood. This study investigated the role of the RASGRP1-S100A9-NLRP3 signaling axis in the cardioprotective effects of S1P. Transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-sequencing analyses were used to identify inflammation-associated candidate genes and their cellular distribution. Male Sprague-Dawley rats received a single intraperitoneal injection of LPS (8 mg/kg) followed by S1P treatment for 6 weeks. Histopathology, echocardiography, serum cardiac-injury markers, oxidative-stress indices, inflammatory cytokines, Western blotting, and cellular metabolic-flux assays were evaluated. RAW264.7 macrophages were used for mechanistic cellular studies. RASGRP1 or NLRP3 overexpression and S100A9-R101Q mutation were used to assess functional contributions. Molecular docking and molecular-dynamics simulations were complemented by SPR, MST, CETSA, DARTS, and Co-IP assays to evaluate S1P-RASGRP1 target engagement and pathway-associated protein interactions. Bioinformatic analyses identified RASGRP1 as a macrophage-enriched, inflammation-associated hub gene. In LPS-treated rats, S1P reduced myocardial inflammatory injury and collagen deposition, improved ejection fraction and fractional shortening, and decreased cardiac-injury, oxidative-stress, and inflammatory markers. In RAW264.7 macrophages, S1P attenuated inflammatory and oxidative-stress responses, restored oxidative phosphorylation and glycolytic capacity, and reduced the abundance of RASGRP1, S100A9, NLRP3, and ASC. SPR and MST supported a concentration-dependent biophysical interaction between S1P and RASGRP1; CETSA and DARTS provided complementary target-stability evidence. The molecular-dynamics trajectory showed substantial rearrangement of S1P from the starting pose before reaching a plateau and therefore supports conformational sampling rather than preservation of the original docked pose. Co-IP supported protein associations within the proposed inflammatory network. RASGRP1 or NLRP3 overexpression attenuated several S1P-associated protective effects. The S100A9-R101Q mutation also weakened several S1P-associated protective responses. SPR indicated a lower apparent dissociation constant for R101Q than for WT S100A9 after model-specific fitting, which is consistent with stronger or more persistent NLRP3 binding rather than loss of the S100A9-NLRP3 interaction. S1P mitigates LPS-induced inflammatory cardiac injury in association with altered macrophage RASGRP1-S100A9-NLRP3 signaling. Biophysical and target-stability assays support direct engagement of RASGRP1 by S1P. However, these findings do not establish RASGRP1 as the sole mediator of S1P activity, exclude contributions from canonical S1P receptor signaling, or demonstrate a strictly linear RASGRP1-S100A9-NLRP3 signaling cascade. Because the LPS model primarily represents endotoxemia-associated inflammatory cardiac injury, extrapolation of these findings to classical viral or autoimmune myocarditis should be made with caution.

papers.title: Computational Optimisation of EtAMA1 Reveals Its Potential as a Vaccine Candidate Against Eimeria tenella.
papers.authors: Rafeer NM, Adeleke VT, Adeleke MA.
papers.abstract: Eimeria tenella is among the most pathogenic chicken-infecting Eimeria species; hence, coccidiosis remains one of the most economically damaging diseases in the poultry industry globally due to poor growth performance, reduced feed efficiency, intestinal pathology, and increased mortality. Conventional control measures, including chemotherapeutic drugs and live-attenuated vaccines, are increasingly limited due to drug resistance, residue concerns, safety concerns, and high production costs, prompting interest in alternative strategies such as apical membrane antigen-1 (AMA1), a conserved and highly immunogenic microneme protein essential for host-cell invasion. Previous studies in Plasmodium, Toxoplasma, and Babesia have demonstrated the successful use of AMA1 in recombinant and immunoinformatic-designed vaccines, underscoring its potential as a cross-species subunit vaccine candidate. This study explored Eimeria tenella AMA1 (EtAMA1) with the aim of investigating the physicochemical and structural properties, identifying antigenic T-cell and B-cell epitopes using immunoinformatic tools and evaluating the effectiveness of EtAMA1 in inducing an immune response within the host. The structural analysis revealed a z-score of -6.86 and a Ramachandran plot of 97.19%. EtAMA1 contained three CD8+, seven CD4+ T-cell epitopes, one linear, and eight discontinuous B-cell epitopes. The ability of EtAMA1 to elicit an immune response was assessed via an in silico immune simulation. The binding interaction energy generated via molecular docking and dynamics simulations indicated a strong binding interaction of EtAMA1 to Toll-like receptor 5. The results indicate that EtAMA1 is a strong vaccine candidate; however, experimental validation is required.

papers.title: Integrating Machine Learning to Identify Prognostic Subtypes and the Cisplatin Resistance Gene RRM2 in Lung Adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Huang H, Tao T, Li Z, Zhai K, Cui B, Feng H, Li P, Li B.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a highly invasive malignancy associated with poor prognosis. However, reliable molecular subtypes and prognostic signatures for LUAD, particularly their associations with tumor immunity and treatment response, remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify distinct molecular subtypes and establish a robust prognostic signature for LUAD, while exploring potential therapeutic targets associated with cisplatin resistance. In this study, we integrated ten clustering algorithms with 101 machine learning methods to identify two distinct molecular subtypes of LUAD and established a robust consensus machine learning-derived signature (CMLS). Patients belonging to the Cluster A subtype exhibited a more favorable prognosis and an enhanced immune response. Furthermore, a CMLS model constructed from 19 genes exhibited strong predictive power. Individuals with high CMLS scores displayed reduced CD4 + T-cell infiltration, poorer survival outcomes, and diminished responses to immunotherapy, whereas those with the low CMLS scores showed improved clinical outcomes, better immunotherapy responsiveness, and features of an immunologically "hot" tumor phenotype. Among the identified genes, ribonucleotide reductase subunit M2 (RRM2) emerged as a core regulator associated with LUAD prognosis. RRM2 was markedly upregulated in lung cancer tissues and the LUAD cell lines and was associated with the cisplatin (DDP) resistance. Suppression of RRM2 expression significantly enhanced the cisplatin sensitivity of A549/DDP cells. In summary, our findings establish a molecular classifier that stratifies LUAD patients into distinct risk categories and highlight RRM2 as a promising biomarker and therapeutic target associated with cisplatin resistance.

papers.title: The influence of LINC00511 and MDM2/MDM4 in lung carcinoma: Implications for immunological therapeutic strategies .
papers.authors: Zhang F, Li Q.
papers.abstract: Background Immunotherapy has significantly improved the treatment of lung cancer, but some patients experience aggressive disease, the mechanisms of which remain unclear. In particular, the interaction between lncRNA and the MDM2/MDM4 pathway warrants in-depth exploration. Objectives This study aimed to investigate the role of LINC00511 in promoting aggressive disease during immunotherapy for lung carcinoma by modulating MDM2/MDM4 expression. Methods This study collected tissues from 30 lung cancer patients undergoing immunotherapy and used A549 cell lines. RT-PCR detected expression of LINC00511, while immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence detected MDM2/MDM4 expression. Bioinformatics analysis and luciferase reporter assays were performed to confirm their relationship. Cell migration, invasion, proliferation and response to PD-1 inhibitors were assessed. Results using A549 cells and female BALB/c nude mice (n=6 per group). LINC00511 was significantly upregulated in aggressive disease tissues and positively correlated with tumor stage. MDM2/MDM4 expression was also elevated (P Conclusion LINC00511 promotes hyperprogressive disease in lung cancer during immunotherapy by upregulating MDM2/MDM4. Inhibition of LINC00511 effectively reverses tumor progression, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: Hepatic Progenitor Cells and the Ductular Reaction: Pathophysiological Role in the Progression of Liver Disease.
papers.authors: Wang P, Li M, Zhou Z, Luo K, Lu Y, Zhang Z, Su J, Zhang S, Tu Y, Luo H, Li Q, Jia X.
papers.abstract: Ductular reaction (DR), a defining histological hallmark of diverse acute and chronic liver injuries, is fundamentally driven by the activation of hepatic progenitor cells (HPCs) and their complex, spatiotemporal bidirectional crosstalk within the hepatic niche. As bipotent precursor cells, HPCs initiate compensatory regeneration when mature hepatocyte proliferation is compromised. However, DR is not a uniform process but a multiphase dynamic reaction: transient early activation facilitates parenchymal restoration, whereas persistent, dysregulated HPC expansion fuels progressive fibrogenesis. The convergence of conserved developmental signalling cascades-including Hippo-YAP, Hedgehog, Notch and TGF-β-strictly governs HPC fate commitment and biliary epithelial proliferation. Concurrently, DR orchestrates intricate inflammatory circuitries by recruiting innate and adaptive immune cells, activating hepatic stellate cells and remodelling the extracellular matrix, thereby establishing a pro-fibrotic niche that perpetuates chronic injury. This review systematically categorizes the disease-specific morphological and molecular subtypes of DR across heterogeneous liver disorders, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), viral hepatitis and cholestatic liver diseases, highlighting its robust value as an independent histological and serological prognostic biomarker. Leveraging recent mechanistic breakthroughs from single-cell transcriptomics, lineage tracing and spatial imaging, we comprehensively evaluate widely adopted preclinical models and summarise emerging therapeutic strategies targeting the HPC-DR axis, such as small-molecule compounds, phytochemicals and cytokine modulators. Despite substantial advances in deciphering the HPC-DR axis, critical translational bottlenecks impede its clinical application. Collectively, this review integrates state-of-the-art multidimensional evidence to reconstruct the pathogenic network of HPC-DR interactions, providing mechanistic insights to facilitate precise prognostic evaluation and the development of novel targeted interventions for chronic liver diseases.
papers.venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver

papers.title: Exploring the Mechanism of Zhigancao Decoction in the Treatment of Chronic Heart Failure via Modulation of Oxidative Stress.
papers.authors: Luo Z, Huang Y, Tian Y, Huang S, Li F.
papers.abstract: Background Zhigancao decoction has shown therapeutic potential in the management of chronic heart failure (CHF); however, the molecular mechanisms underlying its pharmacological effects remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate its potential mechanisms, with a particular focus on oxidative stress-related pathways. Methods The chemical profile of Zhigancao decoction was characterized by LC-MS/MS, and putative targets were predicted using SwissTargetPrediction. A protein-protein interaction (PPI) network was established using the STRING database and Cytoscape software, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses. Differentially expressed genes from two GEO datasets (GSE9128 and GSE84796) were integrated with reactive oxygen species (ROS)-related genes to identify candidate targets. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were subsequently performed to investigate compound-target interactions. Results A total of 66 chemical constituents and 818 putative targets were characterized and collected, respectively. Among these targets, MMP9 emerged as a central candidate associated with the therapeutic effects of Zhigancao decoction. GO and KEGG enrichment analyses demonstrated that the core targets were significantly enriched in oxidative stress-related pathways, inflammatory signaling cascades, and cell fate regulatory pathways. Computational deconvolution of bulk transcriptomic data suggested marked alterations in the estimated immune cell composition of the CHF microenvironment. Network pharmacology analysis further indicated that multiple chemical constituents of Zhigancao decoction converge on MMP9 and its associated pathways. Molecular docking analysis demonstrated favorable binding affinities between 10 representative compounds and MMP9, with binding energies below -7.0 kcal/mol. Conclusions In silico predictions suggest that Zhigancao decoction may exert potential therapeutic effects against CHF through computationally predicted targeting of MMP9 and associated oxidative stress- and immune-related pathways. These computational findings provide a theoretical foundation for future experimental investigations into the mechanisms of Zhigancao decoction in CHF, though clinical application would require confirmation through rigorous in vivo and clinical studies.

papers.title: Divergent T cell programs in plaque rupture and erosion revealed by single-cell multiomics in the OPTICO-ACS study.
papers.authors: Horstmann H, Wolfram C, De Vore L, Abdelwahed YS, Amend A, Meteva D, Heiser M, Stapmanns P, Seppelt C, Zanders L, Nelles G, Peters D, Wientjens C, Zimmermann F, Yücel D, Franitza M, Becker K, Losert C, Heinig M, Stark K, Joner M, Lang A, Riffelmacher T, Gerdes N, Baldus S, Giannarelli C, Wolf D, Landmesser U, Kränkel N, Leistner DM, Winkels H, Gerhardt T.
papers.abstract: Plaque erosion accounts for up to 40% of acute coronary syndromes. Unlike plaque rupture, erosion is characterized by thrombus formation on an intact fibrous cap following endothelial denudation. Rupture is associated with broad inflammatory activation, whereas erosion features accumulation of specific immune cells, particularly CD4+ and CD8+ T cells. Their functional programming remains insufficiently defined.The objective was to characterize intracoronary and peripheral T cell phenotypes, activation programs, and clonal architecture in acute coronary syndromes caused by plaque erosion compared with plaque rupture. We prospectively enrolled 133 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndromes in whom plaque erosion or rupture was classified by optical coherence tomography. Blood was sampled from the coronary segment proximal to the lesion and from the peripheral circulation. T cell phenotypes were assessed by flow cytometry and plasma proteomics. In a subgroup, intracoronary samples underwent CITE-seq, integrating single-cell transcriptomics with surface protein profiling, together with paired T cell receptor sequencing. Flow cytometry demonstrated enrichment of activated memory helper and cytotoxic T cells with anti-inflammatory features at erosion sites, in contrast to predominantly naive and pro-inflammatory T cells in rupture. CITE-seq revealed erosion-specific activation of pathways related to proliferation, adhesion, and tissue repair, whereas T cells in rupture displayed enhanced inflammatory pathways. Functional validation confirmed greater IL-2/IFN-γ induction in rupture-associated memory T cells and greater IL-10 induction in erosion-associated Tregs. T cell receptor sequencing showed greater clonal expansion in erosion, suggesting antigen-experienced clonal selection, whereas rupture exhibited broader and less focused clonal diversity. Plaque erosion and plaque rupture show fundamentally different T cell immune profiles. Erosion is marked by memory-skewed, clonally expanded regulatory and cytotoxic T cell subsets, while rupture is characterized by proinflammatory phenotypes, diverse T cell receptor repertoires, and heightened inflammatory signaling. These findings support morphology-tailored immunotherapeutic approaches, including established anti-inflammatory strategies for rupture and selective T cell-directed interventions for erosion.

papers.title: Development of a novel next-generation multi-epitope vaccine targeting the Guaroa virus glycoprotein precursor through reverse vaccinology.
papers.authors: Asim M, Almatroudi A, Yehia RS, Almustafa H, Aljohani WA, Alrashedi M, Alshuhayb R, Al-Megrin WAI.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop a multi-epitope vaccine candidate against Guaroa virus using integrated immunoinformatics and reverse vaccinology approaches. The viral glycoprotein precursor was selected as the target for epitope screening. Potential B-cell and T-cell epitopes with predicted antigenic properties, non-allergenicity, and non-toxicity were identified through computational analyses. Global population coverage assessment predicted a population coverage of 99.09% based on the selected HLA-associated epitopes. Selected epitopes were assembled into a chimeric vaccine construct containing β-defensin-3 adjuvant and linker sequences. Physicochemical analysis predicted properties relevant to solubility and recombinant expression, although these characteristics require experimental assessment. Structural prediction and refinement yielded a model in which 99.5% of residues were located within favored regions. Molecular docking predicted interactions between the vaccine construct and immune receptors TLR2, TLR3, and TLR4, with TLR4 showing the lowest docking score among the three receptors. Molecular dynamics simulations were used to assess the predicted structural behavior of the vaccine-receptor complexes. The vaccine-TLR4 complex yielded a docking score of -1212.9, while MM-GBSA analysis produced a ΔG_bind estimate of -227.14 kcal/mol based on the final trajectory frame. Immune simulation predicted increases in antibody production, cytokine release, and memory cell formation. Collectively, these findings support the computational prioritization of the construct as a vaccine candidate for further experimental investigation, although experimental and clinical validation remain necessary.

papers.title: Development of a multi-organ single-cell atlas of systemic sclerosis reveals shared and tissue-specific pathogenic pathways.
papers.authors: Iperi, C.; Geiss, C.; Lugar, M.; Stauffer, P.; Vlachogiannis, N.; Hofman, A.; Khmelevskaya, A.; Sfikakis, P. P.; Hoffmann-Vold, A.-M.; Micheroli, R.; Seiler, C.; Distler, O.; Ospelt, C.; Elhai, M.
papers.abstract: Objectives: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a multi-organ autoimmune disease for which no broadly effective disease-modifying treatment exists. We developed an integrated multi-organ single-cell atlas of SSc to identify shared and organ specific disease-associated transcriptional programmes and potential therapeutic targets. Methods: We integrated single-cell RNA-sequencing data from skin, lung, synovium, and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (six studies, 401,902 cells, 90 individuals) using Harmony. Pseudobulk differential expression and gene set enrichment analysis were performed at the tissue cell-compartment, cell-type, and subpopulation levels, including independent reclustering of lymphoid, myeloid and fibroblast populations. Results: Disease-associated transcriptional programmes showed marked tissue dependence, even within the same cell lineage, highlighting the importance of organ-specific mechanisms in SSc. Nevertheless, recurrent extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling programmes were identified in lung, skin and synovium, and interferon signalling programmes in skin, synovium and peripheral blood mononuclear cells, across immune and fibroblast cell populations. Although no subpopulation was exclusive to SSc, a shared myofibroblast subpopulation expressing SFRP2, COL1A1, POSTN, ACTA2, and COMP was identified across lung, skin, and synovium. In addition, perivascular and mitotic fibroblast subpopulations exhibited both profibrotic and inflammatory signatures, including interferon- and IL-2-related signalling programmes. Conclusions: SSc is characterised by two complementary axes: a tissue-dependent cellular programme and a recurrent fibrotic and interferon-associated signature extending across multiple organs and cell populations. These findings are consistent with current organ-based therapeutic approaches while highlighting interferon signalling as a potential multi-organ therapeutic target. The resulting interactive single-cell atlas provides a resource for investigating shared and organ-specific disease mechanisms and guiding future therapeutic research.

papers.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3.
papers.authors: Woods LJ, Neff B, Lahouel K, Goursaud A, Mulazimoglu M, Bates K, Tomasetti C, Altin JA.
papers.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against "unseen" epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000 TCRs mapped to >1000 distinct epitopes restricted by >70 MHC class I/II alleles, we identify features that distinguish cognate triads from controls. The resulting model achieves median areas under the curve of 0.81 to 0.92 on validation triads unseen by AF3 or during feature selection. Our results reveal that generalized prediction of TCR specificity from sequence is possible, with the potential to greatly accelerate the decoding of immune responses.

papers.title: LILRB3 as an ulcerative colitis-associated molecular biomarker: integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental validation.
papers.authors: Yang B, Sun D, Liu Z, Zhou L.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease characterized by mucosal inflammation and immune dysregulation. Although macrophage-mediated inflammation is associated with UC progression, its molecular basis remains incompletely understood. This study integrated bioinformatic analyses and experimental validation to identify UC-associated molecular biomarkers and explore their roles in immune dysregulation. Bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated for differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), and multi-algorithm machine learning. The machine-learning model was evaluated in independent validation cohorts, and a nomogram was subsequently constructed and evaluated in an additional colonic-tissue cohort. Immune infiltration, single-cell RNA sequencing, cell-cell communication, pseudotime analysis, and scTenifoldKnk-based virtual knockout were used to investigate hub genes. RT-qPCR, WB, and IHC validated the findings in a DSS-induced mouse model and clinical samples, while siRNA-mediated LILRB3 knockdown was performed in THP-1-derived macrophages. Differential expression analysis and WGCNA identified 55 candidate genes. Through screening of 127 machine-learning algorithm combinations, DPP10, LILRB3, MTMR11, and SLC6A14 were identified as UC-associated molecular biomarkers. A separately constructed logistic regression nomogram showed an apparent AUC of 0.989. LILRB3 was predominantly expressed in myeloid cells, particularly M1 macrophages, and was associated with inflammatory immune cell infiltration. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed that LILRB3⁺ M1 macrophages exhibited active intercellular communication involving MHC-II-CD4 and other inflammation-related signaling pathways. Experimental validation showed increased PirB expression in the colonic tissues of DSS-induced colitis mice and elevated LILRB3 expression in human UC colonic tissues. Knockdown of LILRB3 in THP-1-derived macrophages significantly reduced TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β mRNA expression. LILRB3 is a candidate UC-associated molecular biomarker in colonic tissue and may be associated with proinflammatory macrophage remodeling and myeloid immune dysregulation, warranting mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: Repurposing the orphan drug nitisinone synergizes with sorafenib to sensitize immunotherapy-refractory MSS-CRC via metabolic stress-driven STING activation.
papers.authors: Wu M, Tang G, Liu M, Wang X, Xie Y, Wu Y, Lin J, Weng J, Wang X, Yu H, Huang M, Yuan S, Luo Y, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS-CRC) remains broadly refractory to immune checkpoint blockade, underscoring the need for strategies that convert immunologically "cold" tumors into therapy-responsive states. Here, we identify 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase (HPD), the rate-limiting enzyme in tyrosine catabolism, as a modulator of sorafenib sensitivity in MSS-CRC. Pharmacological inhibition of HPD by the FDA-approved orphan drug nitisinone synergized with sorafenib across patient-derived organoids, human PBMC-tumor co-cultures, and immunocompetent orthotopic models. Mechanistically, nitisinone imposes strict glutaminolysis dependency, whereas sorafenib disrupts cRaf-MEK-ERK signaling to trigger proteasomal cMYC degradation and transcriptional repression of GLS1, thereby ablating compensatory glutamine anaplerosis. This dual metabolic blockade creates a synthetic lethal trap, provoking irreversible mitochondrial collapse and mtDNA release, which activates the cGAS-STING pathway and drives intratumoral infiltration of cytotoxic NK and CD8+ T cells. Critically, ρ⁰ cells and STING-deficient models confirm mitochondrial damage as the "trigger" of cell death and STING as the "amplifier" of antitumor immunity. In TCGA MSS-CRC cohorts, a double-low glutamine/tyrosine metabolic signature was associated with prolonged survival, enhanced cGAS-STING signaling, and immune-hot tumor features, findings corroborated by single-cell RNA-seq analyses. Finally, the triple combination of nitisinone, sorafenib, and anti-PD-1 therapy achieved superior antitumor efficacy with favorable tolerability in vivo. Collectively, our findings delineate a metabolic-mitochondrial-STING axis and support repurposing nitisinone as a promising translational strategy to sensitize MSS-CRC to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Decoder-FFPE-seq enables sensitive, genome-wide spatial transcriptomics of archival tissues at single-cell resolution.
papers.authors: Cao J, Zeng J, Meng Y, Huang S, Zhang J, Fang X, Guo Y, Shi W, Liu Y, Zheng Z, Fang J, Xiong X, Chen G, Wu L, Yang C.
papers.abstract: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissue-compatible spatial transcriptomics (ST) is transforming biology and histopathology, but achieving high sensitivity, genome-wide coverage, single-cell resolution, and researcher accessibility remains challenging. To address these challenges, we here present a dendrimeric DNA coordinate barcoding design for FFPE tissue-adapted spatial RNA sequencing (Decoder-FFPE-seq) by integrating RNA-to-DNA probe conversion with blotting-assisted barcoding. Decoder-FFPE-seq provides single-cell resolution with a >2.6-fold sensitivity increase in whole-transcriptome mouse brain and archived human sample profiling over existing platforms, resolving potential cellular identity of low-abundance genes, finer tissue architecture, and capturing an epithelial-mesenchymal transition-associated signature for prognostic value. With expanded probe libraries, Decoder-FFPE-seq captures long noncoding and viral RNAs, revealing their spatial coregulatory networks with messenger RNAs in oral squamous cell carcinomas (OSCCs). In an OSCC immunotherapy cohort, two CD8+ T cell subpopulations were respectively identified in pre- and postchemoimmunotherapy samples, potentially linked to treatment response. Decoder-FFPE-seq establishes a robust, high-resolution, and accessible framework for sensitive ST profiling of archival tissues in fundamental and translational studies.

papers.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
papers.authors: Wyler E, Albertini S, Friedel CC, Manukyan A, Winterfeldt A, Bracker N, Huang J, Krasemann S, Plumbom I, Altmüller J, Conrad T, Reimer R, Schneider C, Radbruch H, Hafezi W, Hansen A, Grundhoff A, Landthaler M, Fischer N, Czech-Sioli M.
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. To model this complex environment, we used human hair-bearing skin organoids and combined single-cell spatial transcriptomics with imaging to map viral spread and host responses across skin architecture. Our data suggest delayed progression of the HSV-1 life cycle in epidermal keratinocytes and hair follicle cells compared to the dermis. Infection triggered spatially organized host responses, including induction of IER3 in papillary fibroblasts. In basal keratinocytes, IRF3 was up-regulated in both infected and neighboring uninfected cells, consistent with paracrine activation of antiviral signaling. Inflammatory responses were compartmentalized in a cell type-specific manner, with TNFSF9 (4-1BBL) induced in papillary fibroblasts and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α) induced in keratinocytes. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays confirmed secretion of these cytokines and the TNF-α-responsive chemokines CXCL2 and CXCL10. CXCL2 expression was enriched in cells adjacent to TNF-α-expressing cells, highlighting spatial coordination of inflammatory signaling. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

papers.title: Neoantigen evolution in cancer: immunoediting, immune escape, and future vaccine strategies.
papers.authors: Martínez-Cortés F, Valle JG, Maruri J, Martínez-Zarco BA, Domínguez-Romero AN, Gevorkian G, Manoutcharian K.
papers.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has changed cancer treatment, with neoantigen-based vaccines emerging as a promising strategy to induce tumor-specific immune responses while minimizing adverse effects on healthy tissues. Advances in next-generation sequencing, immunopeptidomics, artificial intelligence, and computational prediction have accelerated the identification of patient-specific neoantigens and enabled the development of personalized cancer vaccines. Despite encouraging safety profiles and robust induction of neoantigen-specific T-cell responses, clinical efficacy has remained inconsistent. Tumor evolution driven by genomic instability continuously reshapes the neoantigen landscape through intratumoral heterogeneity, immune-mediated selection, and antigen gain or loss, facilitating immune escape and limiting durable therapeutic responses. In addition, T-cell dysfunction and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment further compromise vaccine efficacy. In this review, we discuss the origin and diversity of tumor antigens, recent advances in neoantigen identification and vaccine development, and the biological mechanisms that constrain the clinical success of personalized cancer vaccines. We summarize evidence from clinical trials that highlights both the promise and the current limitations of neoantigen-based immunotherapy, and discuss the importance of incorporating tumor evolution into vaccine design. Finally, we present Variable Epitope Libraries (VELs), a vaccine strategy that uses immunogens based on combinatorial libraries of highly mutated epitope variants designed to broaden immune recognition, reduce immune escape, and improve the durability and effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy.
papers.venue: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Reviews on cancer

papers.title: CMTM6 regulates hematopoietic stem cell homeostasis through modulating IFNRs-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis.
papers.authors: Qiu H, He W, Feng Y, Wang B, Zheng L, Pan C, Qiu Q, Sun Y, Cui X, Wang J, Su A, Su Z, Hu Y.
papers.abstract: CMTM6 is known to stabilize PD-L1 on cancer cells, facilitating immune evasion, but its role in normal hematopoiesis remains unexplored. Hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) homeostasis is tightly regulated by interferon (IFN) signaling, yet the mechanisms controlling IFN receptor stability are unclear. In this study we investigated whether CMTM6 regulates HSC maintenance and elucidated the underlying molecular pathways. Using a conditional Cmtm6 knockout mouse model (Vav-Cre), we performed flow cytometry, competitive transplantation, single-cell RNA sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, and functional assays on bone marrow HSCs. Cmtm6 deficiency led to increased HSC proliferation but impaired reconstitution capacity, accompanied by elevated DNA damage and disrupted cell polarity. Single-cell analysis revealed a marked reduction in IFN response pathways. Mechanistically, CMTM6 directly interacted with IFNAR1 and IFNGR1, stabilizing their protein expression. Downstream, Cmtm6 deletion impaired STAT1 phosphorylation and reduced KLF4 expression; single-cell analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between Stat1 activity and Klf4 expression, and STAT1 inhibition in HSCs confirmed that STAT1 activity is required for maintaining KLF4 expression. Notably, KLF4 overexpression partially rescued colony-forming defects and reduced γH2AX foci in Cmtm6-deficient HSCs, identifying KLF4 as a key downstream effector. Additionally, we observed accompanying molecular changes including reduced SIAH2, elevated DYRK2, decreased c-MYC, and increased P53, which may contribute to the observed phenotypes. These findings demonstrate that CMTM6 maintains HSC homeostasis by stabilizing IFN receptors and regulating the IFNR-STAT1-KLF4 signaling axis, revealing a novel physiological function for CMTM6 in hematopoiesis.

papers.title: Clinical and metabolic subtypes of recent-onset adult type 1 diabetes: a prospective cohort study.
papers.authors: Prystupa K, Fritsche A, Binsch C, Lanzinger S, Szczerbinski L, Janucik A, Kretowski AJ, Zaharia OP, Heilmann G, Trinks N, Huttasch M, Straßburger K, Bönhof G, Strom A, Guthoff R, Haider SMI, Dilthey A, Marschall T, Bódis K, Burkart V, Seissler J, Szendroedi J, Mai K, Stumvoll M, Meyhöfer S, Birkenfeld AL, Holl RW, Heni M, Roden M, Wagner R, German Diabetes Study (GDS) group.
papers.abstract: Adult-onset type 1 diabetes exhibits substantial heterogeneity. We aimed to investigate whether this variability reflects distinct disease entities or different temporal stages of a shared autoimmune process. In this prospective cohort study, we analysed data from adults (aged 18-69 years) in the German Diabetes Study who had clinically diagnosed type 1 diabetes within the preceding 12 months, and from individuals who were positive for glutamic acid decarboxylase antibody (GADA) but had originally been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes. We used unsupervised machine learning based on GADA status, fasting C-peptide, glucose, triglycerides, and HDL cholesterol to characterise clinical and metabolic type 1 diabetes subtypes. The resulting subtypes were compared for aetiological traits (polygenic risk scores for type 1 diabetes and type 2 diabetes, partitioned type 2 diabetes polygenic risk scores, human leukocyte antigen [HLA] profiles, and islet-directed autoantibodies), insulin sensitivity, glucagon-stimulated C-peptide trajectories as a measure of residual β-cell function, and complications during prospective follow-up. Reproducibility was assessed in adults with type 1 diabetes from the German Diabetes Prospective Follow-up Registry (Diabetes-Patienten-Verlaufsdokumentation [DPV]). Analysed participants in the German Diabetes Study cohort were recruited between June 27, 2005, and Jan 20, 2025 (n=600), and were followed up for a mean of 6·1 (SD 4·7) years. We identified three type 1 diabetes subtypes: two GADA-positive subtypes, and one GADA-negative subtype. A similar clinical and metabolic subtype structure was observed in the DPV cohort, whose participants were recruited between 2000 and 2025 (n=483) and were followed up for a mean of 3·1 (SD 5·0) years. One GADA-positive subtype was characterised by lower BMI, higher insulin sensitivity, and severe β-cell dysfunction (classic type 1 diabetes), whereas the second showed higher BMI, lower insulin sensitivity, and better β-cell function (mixed type 1 diabetes). The two GADA-positive subtypes did not differ in autoimmunity or type 1 diabetes polygenic risk scores, whereas the GADA-negative subtype had lower genetic type 1 diabetes risk, despite no clear subtype-specific differences in HLA risk haplotypes. Longitudinal modelling indicated that the mixed type 1 diabetes group was positioned 6·1 years (95% CI 4·6-7·8) earlier along the β-cell function decline trajectory compared with the classic type 1 diabetes group. The risks of hypoglycaemia (log-rank p=0·0019), retinopathy (mixed type 1 diabetes vs classic type 1 diabetes: adjusted hazard ratio 4·93 [95% CI 1·71-14·24]), and cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy (log-rank p=0·028) differed across the groups. Our results indicate that individuals with combined autoimmunity and lower insulin sensitivity present with clinical diabetes earlier than classic type 1 diabetes along the β-cell decline trajectory, identifying a potential timeframe for disease-modifying interventions in specific type 1 diabetes subtypes. BreakthroughT1D, German Research Foundation (DFG), German Center for Diabetes Research (DZD), Schmutzler Stiftung, German Federal Ministry of Health, Ministry of Culture and Science of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, and German Federal Ministry of Education and Research. For the German translation of the abstract see Supplementary Materials section.

papers.title: Exploratory transcriptomic and network pharmacology prioritization of candidate targets and phytochemicals in vascular cognitive impairment.
papers.authors: Alshabrmi FM.
papers.abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) is closely associated with cerebral small vessel disease and is linked to increased disability, institutionalization and mortality, highlighting the need to identify biologically relevant therapeutic candidates. This study applied an exploratory transcriptomic and network pharmacology framework to prioritize candidate targets and phytochemicals relevant to VCI-associated molecular dysfunction. Analysis of the GSE201482 whole-blood dataset identified 1163 nominally differentially expressed genes between VCI and SCD/SVD comparator samples. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified trend-associated turquoise and green modules, yielding 352 overlapping DEG--WGCNA candidate genes. Integration with medicinal plant-derived compound targets identified 52 common candidate genes. Functional enrichment linked these genes to membrane-potential regulation, synaptic compartments, G-protein-coupled receptor signalling, oxidative stress response, hypoxia response, neuroactive ligand signalling and amino-acid metabolism. Immune deconvolution provided exploratory immune-context information on macrophage, monocyte, NK cell and T cell populations. Machine-learning feature prioritization using LASSO, Random Forest and SVM-RFE identified ACP1, CDC25A and MAO-B as candidate genes selected by all three algorithms. External assessment using the independent GSE303449 human brain RNA-seq dataset added a validation layer for candidate interpretation, although FDR-level support for the 52-gene signature and ML-derived panels was limited. MAO-B was selected for docking because it is a druggable neuroactive enzyme with established inhibitor biology and an experimentally resolved ligand-bound structure, enabling reference-based comparison with rasagiline. Docking analysis highlighted isorhamnetin, quercetin and oroxylin A as top-ranked phytochemicals against MAO-B. Overall, this study provides a reproducible candidate-prioritization workflow for guiding future experimental evaluation of multi-target phytochemical approaches in VCI.

papers.title: Codon optimization as a design variable in biotherapeutics.
papers.authors: Jankowska KI, Katneni UK, Stauft CB, Kimchi-Sarfaty C.
papers.abstract: Codon optimization (CO) is a key design variable in biotherapeutics that is used to enhance expression of recombinant proteins, gene therapies, and vaccines. Although synonymous codon substitutions were historically considered neutral, codon choice can influence messenger RNA (mRNA) stability, translation kinetics, cotranslational folding, and immunogenicity. Current optimization strategies integrate computational parameters including codon adaptation indices, tRNA availability, mRNA structure, cytosine-phosphate-guanine dinucleotide content, codon pair bias, and machine learning approaches to balance expression and product quality. Additionally, dynamic tRNA modifications within the epitranscriptome modulate codon-biased translation in a context-dependent manner. While CO has not been implicated in adverse clinical outcomes, its context-dependent effects on protein conformation, post-translational modifications, and immune responses necessitate rigorous characterization. This opinion article presents our viewpoint on mechanisms, applications, and regulatory considerations for CO in biologics.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq analysis reveals a LCR-related prognostic signature for precision prognostication and therapeutic stratification in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Zhong W, Rao R, Zhang J, Cheng M, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Lysine crotonylation (LCR) is an emerging post-translational modification, yet its clinical significance and therapeutic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) remain poorly understood. Multi-omics data were collected from public repositories. Consensus clustering based on 18 LCR-related genes (LCRGs) was performed to define molecular subtypes. Co-expression modules identified via WGCNA were integrated into 101 machine-learning combinations to establish a LCR-related signature (LCRS). The signature was evaluated for survival prediction, immune microenvironment characteristics, and drug response across multiple cohorts, complemented by single-cell RNA sequencing. Candidate therapeutic targets and compounds were screened using DepMap CRISPR dependency data and pharmacogenomic databases (CTRP and PRISM). Two distinct molecular subtypes (C1 and C2) were identified, displaying significant differences in survival, immune infiltration, and signaling pathways. Integrating WGCNA hub genes with an optimal machine-learning framework yielded a robust 15-gene LCRS, which served as an independent prognostic factor in the TCGA cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized signature genes predominantly to endothelial cells. Pharmacogenomic profiling indicated higher sensitivity to sunitinib among high-risk patients, whereas low-risk patients displayed elevated sensitivity to axitinib and pazopanib. Furthermore, dependency screening prioritized CLCNKA as a key therapeutic target along with ten candidate compounds for high-risk patients. This study establishes a robust LCR-related prognostic signature and nominates CLCNKA as a novel therapeutic vulnerability, offering actionable insights for personalized stratification and treatment in ccRCC.

papers.title: Protocol for generating human organoid tumor transplantation and immune-human organoid tumor transplantation models for glioblastoma research.
papers.authors: Li MX, Ge W, Fazzari E, Bhaduri A, Baisiwala S.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma research requires human models that preserve tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions. Here, we present a protocol for generating the human organoid tumor transplantation (HOTT) model and its immunocompetent counterpart, the immune-HOTT (iHOTT) model. These platforms use direct-from-patient tumor cells engrafted into organoids to recapitulate the tumor microenvironment and, in the iHOTT system, autologous tumor-immune interactions. We describe steps for organoid generation, patient tumor dissociation, co-culture with autologous peripheral blood mononuclear cells, fluorescence-activated cell sorting, and downstream single-cell RNA sequencing. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Ge et al. and Baisiwala et al.1,2.

papers.title: Immunity and inflammation in classic Hodgkin lymphoma: Bridging diagnosis, prognosis and precision medicine.
papers.authors: Carbone A, Gloghini A, Ahmed S, Moskowitz A.
papers.abstract: Classic Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) is a unique B-cell malignancy characterized by a small number of malignant Hodgkin and Reed-Sternberg (HRS) cells embedded within an extensive and highly organized inflammatory microenvironment. Recent studies have highlighted that the biological behavior of cHL is largely determined by dynamic interactions between HRS cells and surrounding immune populations, including CD4+ T cells, regulatory T cells, macrophages, eosinophils, mast cells, natural killer cells, and stromal elements. HRS cells actively reshape the tumor microenvironment through the secretion of chemokines and cytokines, including CCL17, CCL22, IL-6, IL-10, and TGF-β, promoting immune cell recruitment, chronic inflammation, and immune tolerance. Concurrently, genetic alterations affecting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis, antigen-presentation pathways, and key signaling cascades such as NF-κB and JAK/STAT facilitate immune escape and tumor persistence. We distinguish diagnostic, prognostic, predictive, and response-monitoring applications and grade biomarkers as established (immunophenotyping, EBER, clinical scores, interim PET), clinically promising (serum TARC, circulating tumor DNA), or investigational (PD-L1-based prediction, spatial and single-cell profiling, artificial intelligence). A deeper understanding of the interplay between immunity and inflammation in cHL may refine disease classification and guide the development of novel immunomodulatory strategies aimed at improving long-term outcomes and overcoming resistance to current therapies.

papers.title: Toll-like receptor 9 agonist IMO-2125 rapidly reshapes the B-cell receptor repertoire in non-human primates.
papers.authors: Xu Y, Zong X, Wang S, Luo L, Wang IM, Zhou Y.
papers.abstract: CpG oligodeoxynucleotides activate Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) and are used as vaccine adjuvants and immunotherapies, but their in vivo effects on the B-cell receptor (BCR) repertoire are incompletely defined. We administered the TLR9 agonist IMO-2125 to Indian rhesus macaques and African green monkeys and profiled peripheral-blood BCR repertoires at baseline, 24 h, 72 h, and 1 week. Light-chain clonotype and lineage diversity decreased after dosing, with the strongest lineage redistribution at 72 h. Most affected lineages decreased in frequency or clonotype number while showing increased mutation rates. Enriched heavy-chain lineages were biased toward mutated IgA and IgG and were consistent with memory- and effector-like B cells. The heavy-chain repertoire was comparatively stable, and responses differed in magnitude between species. These findings indicate that IMO-2125 rapidly reshapes the circulating BCR repertoire, most plausibly through selective redistribution of antigen-experienced B cells rather than broad clonal expansion.

papers.title: SLC11A1 upregulation mediates the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma and decreased sensitivity to cisplatin by mediating macrophage M2 polarization.
papers.authors: Zhou R, Ruan L, Wu C, Lin C, Xie H, Wan Z, Zhu M, Hu X.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated expression of Solute Carrier Family 11 Member 1 (SLC11A1) has been found to be dysregulated in multiple human cancers and is implicated in tumor progression. However, the precise functions and underlying mechanisms of SLC11A1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains largely unknown. Transcriptomic data from HCC patients were analyzed via bioinformatics approaches (co-expression network profiling, functional enrichment) to explore SLC11A1 expression, immune infiltration, and biological functions. Functional assays were performed to validate its roles in HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth. The effect of SLC11A1 on cisplatin sensitivity was evaluated. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunofluorescence were carried out to assess tumor cell proliferation and macrophage polarization markers in tumor tissues. Western blot and rescue experiments with JAK2/STAT3 inhibitors were conducted to explore the underlying mechanism. SLC11A1 expression was altered in HCC tissues based on bioinformatics analysis, and its high expression correlated with poorer survival of patients with HCC. Functionally, SLC11A1 overexpression promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and tumor growth, whereas its knockdown suppressed these malignant phenotypes and enhanced cisplatin sensitivity. SLC11A1 upregulation was associated with immune cell infiltration. SLC11A1 overexpression promoted M2 polarization while inhibiting M1 polarization of macrophages, while SLC11A1 downregulation showed the opposite effects on macrophage polarization. Mechanistically, SLC11A1 upregulation promoted IL-6 and S100A9 expression, and enhanced the phosphorylation of JAK2 and STAT3. Inhibition of JAK2/STAT3 reversed the oncogenic effects of SLC11A1 upregulation. An CONCLUSION: SLC11A1 upregulation is associated with enhanced malignant behaviors, reduced cisplatin sensitivity, and M2 macrophage polarization in HCC potentially through mediating the IL-6/JAK2/STAT3/S100A9 axis.
